chunk_findings.detail: `sync_attributes()` was written to be self-sufficient — it handles a missing `.gitattributes` (`text = attrs.read_text(...) if attrs.exists() else ""`) — but its new caller refuses to run it unless the file already exists *and already contains* a `merge=pinsregen` line. So `pins regenerate` can never bootstrap the file or add the first line: given a repo whose `.gitattributes` has no `merge=pinsregen` line at all (a fresh clone of a repo that relies on the claim's shared `info/attributes` for driver wiring, or any repo configured with `[pins] after_merge = "off"`), the caller silently does nothing — and with `after_merge = "off"`, `install()` returns before `sync_attributes()` (`if not files or cfg.pins.after_merge == "off": return []`), so *no* code path writes attributes in that configuration. `ddflow pins regenerate` leaves the doctor warning in place, and the only remaining way to get the line is `pins regenerate --install`, i.e. exactly the command that writes the post-merge hook the change exists to avoid. The docstring of `sync_attributes` ("Add the merge=pinsregen line of every recipe file .gitattributes lacks") and the change's stated intent are not delivered by any reachable path for that input.

chunk_findings.detail: The only invocation that runs without a human is the post-merge hook, whose body is `pins regenerate --after-merge`; the new gate explicitly skips syncing for `after_merge`, so after a merge that brings in a recipe whose attribute line is missing, the worktree's committed `.gitattributes` is still not brought in step — the hook re-records pins but leaves the very drift the change targets. Fixing it still requires manually running plain `pins regenerate` (or `--install`, which rewrites the hook). The diff gives no comment or test for why `--after-merge` is excluded, and the new test only exercises the plain path, so the exclusion is also untested.

commit: budget_findings, per-tier report, tiers full-list assert removed

chunk_findings.detail: The change implements only the pytest half of D-mcp-budget-report. The diff contains no non-test code at all, so the per-tier numbers are still not "REPORTED (doctor, brief, SE-mcp-budget)" as the decision requires, and the task's own acceptance ("doctor and brief show the per-tier numbers") is not met. Concretely: after this lands, `ddflow doctor` and `ddflow brief` print the same single tools/list number (or nothing) they printed before; the only place core/standard/all sizes appear is inside one pytest test's `warnings.warn` output, which an operator who is not reading the pytest warnings summary never sees. The intent states those bodies may drop the "add no MCP tool, ~45 bytes of headroom" boilerplate "once DX-tools-list-budget-headroom lands" — but with the production reporting absent, nothing operator-facing actually reports the budget, so the ratchet-removal is only visible to CI.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py:``test_tools_list_bytes_per_tier_are_reported`` / ``budget_findings`` [D-mcp-budget-report]

chunk_findings.detail: The "warn instead of fail" behaviour depends on the warning filter staying non-fatal. Under an environment where pytest is run with `-W error`, or where `pyproject.toml`/`pytest.ini` sets `filterwarnings = ["error"]` (a common strict-CI setting), `warnings.warn` raises `UserWarning` at that line and `test_tools_list_bytes_per_tier_are_reported` fails whenever any tier exceeds `TOOLS_LIST_BUDGET` — i.e. the build fails for exactly the over-budget condition D-mcp-budget-report says must only be reported. A robust implementation would not rely on the ambient filter (e.g. a recorded/report-only assertion channel that cannot be escalated to an exception).

chunk_findings.detail: The change implements only the pytest half of D-mcp-budget-report. The diff contains no non-test code at all, so the per-tier numbers are still not "REPORTED (doctor, brief, SE-mcp-budget)" as the decision requires, and the task's own acceptance ("doctor and brief show the per-tier numbers") is not met. Concretely: after this lands, `ddflow doctor` and `ddflow brief` print the same single tools/list number (or nothing) they printed before; the only place core/standard/all sizes appear is inside one pytest test's `warnings.warn` output, which an operator who is not reading the pytest warnings summary never sees. The intent states those bodies may drop the "add no MCP tool, ~45 bytes of headroom" boilerplate "once DX-tools-list-budget-headroom lands" — but with the production reporting absent, nothing operator-facing actually reports the budget, so the ratchet-removal is only visible to CI.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py:``test_tools_list_bytes_per_tier_are_reported`` / ``budget_findings`` [D-mcp-budget-report]

chunk_findings.detail: The "warn instead of fail" behaviour depends on the warning filter staying non-fatal. Under an environment where pytest is run with `-W error`, or where `pyproject.toml`/`pytest.ini` sets `filterwarnings = ["error"]` (a common strict-CI setting), `warnings.warn` raises `UserWarning` at that line and `test_tools_list_bytes_per_tier_are_reported` fails whenever any tier exceeds `TOOLS_LIST_BUDGET` — i.e. the build fails for exactly the over-budget condition D-mcp-budget-report says must only be reported. A robust implementation would not rely on the ambient filter (e.g. a recorded/report-only assertion channel that cannot be escalated to an exception).
